items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (windowSql, buildWindowSpecSql, resolvedSpec). Each .window() method has a JSDoc block, and the formatting matches the existing builders. The manual chunk loop is wordier than sql.join but still easy to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Name validation and the function-spec Proxy resolution are copied into all 5 select.ts files instead of a shared helper like assertValidWindowName. The WINDOW chunk loop is also copied 5 times. Helpers went in sql/expressions/window.ts, not sql/functions as the conventions ask.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: All required checks are present and tested: empty and whitespace window names, ntile/nthValue positive integers, preceding/following non-negative integers, and frame from/to ordering. Numeric arguments are emitted inline, never as bound params. Minor issue: casts like `resolvedSpec as any`.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: Purely additive: an optional `windows?:` field on every *SelectConfig and the same .window() on pg, mysql, sqlite, gel and singlestore. windowSql is undefined when no window is defined, so existing SQL is unchanged. All 566 existing (P2P) tests pass.
